criteria.always_lazy: The ingress layer never prefetches: each handler triggers the single consumption of its request payload. Buffered accessors pull the stream into memory within the cap, while the reader operation exposes the untouched wire stream directly. Payloads beyond the cap appear as domain failures the handler must translate, so an automatic 413 disappears.
criteria.eager_only: Ingress keeps filling its bounded buffer ahead of every dispatch, still answering oversize payloads with an automatic 413 before any handler executes. Reader handles wrap the buffered copy, which bounds memory by the cap but never observes the wire incrementally; the contract states that ceiling openly.
criteria.route_marked: Each route declares its appetite in advance through a marker: ordinary routes retain prefetch ingress plus the automatic pre-handler 413, and marked routes defer every byte until the handler pulls them through a single stream reader. The marker is the only new catalogue item in this path.

body_mode.instructions: Where should the buffered-versus-live decision live for request payloads?

criteria.buffered_repeatable: Memory-backed accessors remain freely repeatable, and the reader operation may be used at most once per request. After a live reader opens, memory accessors report the body consumed. When buffered access happened first, the reader replays the retained bytes instead of touching the wire.
criteria.mode_exclusive: Whichever style touches the body first becomes the request's permanent style: buffered access pins buffered style, reader creation pins live style, and any later access in the other style fails. Repeats are fine inside buffered style; the live reader opens a single time.
criteria.single_shot: The body is a one-use resource no matter the accessor: buffered reads, decodes and reader creation each exhaust it, and every repeat attempt fails. Handlers capture the payload once into a local binding.

consumption.instructions: What repeat and mixing discipline should body accessors obey?

criteria.callback_fold: Handlers supply status, headers and a generation callback to a single operation that pumps the callback, frames its output, and settles the wire stream. Chunk handles never surface in handler code.
criteria.reader_pipe: Handlers attach a ready-made stream reader to a status and headers, and the adapter relays that reader onto the wire. The responding handler composes sources rather than emitting chunks.
criteria.writer_pair: Handlers first build a pending response, then claim its writer a single time through a companion operation, emit chunks with the common write operation, close, and return the response for dispatch.

response_stream.instructions: Which production shape fits streaming responses?

criteria.arg_send: Handlers call a send operation carrying writer, data, event, id and retry as separate parameters, with empties standing for absent fields. No dedicated event value is declared.
criteria.raw_stream: The catalogue gains nothing event-specific: handlers serialize the event-stream framing by hand with byte writes and accept responsibility for its exactness.
criteria.record_send: The catalogue declares one event record holding data, event, id and retry, where empty stands for absent. A send operation checks framing and rejects embedded line breaks, and a comment operation emits heartbeat remarks.

sse_shape.instructions: How should event-stream emission be packaged?

state: The Can web stack runs on Bun.serve pinned at 1.4.2. Current ingress prefetches every request payload into a bounded buffer ahead of dispatch, oversize payloads get an automatic 413 with zero handler involvement, and buffered body, JSON and form accessors replay from retained bytes; tests pin all three facts. Reusable B1-05 pull handles exist: opaque byte readers plus writers offering read_many with a per-chunk ceiling, write_some with accepted counts, close and cancel, zero prefetch, and no running total ceiling. The B1-06 brief demands wire-incremental request ingestion through read_many under per-chunk ceilings, surfacing chunk order, authentic connection drops, framing breaches and consumption breaches; repeat reads of an exhausted body must fail; sluggish clients must throttle response buffering via backpressure; the route table must span PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS and HEAD; TLS plus Server-Sent Events are in scope. Recorded probes show: request.body streams live and ignoring it never stalls the reply; cancel followed by a reply succeeds; a dropped client rejects the pending server read with AbortError alongside the request signal; HEAD payloads vanish natively; header listings already separate Set-Cookie in both directions; an error halfway through a response arrives as a quietly shortened 200. Standing rules: extend the catalogue only, never the grammar; the automatic-413 and replayable-read pins stand unless this decision deliberately relocates them; ownership remains open to closing to closed with per-request handle scope; measured acceptance beats this guidance.
